newsitem.title: UK: No relief for platinum, palladium market tensions.
newsitem.headline: No relief for platinum, palladium market tensions.

text.p: Prices of the rare precious metals platinum and palladium remained at dizzy heights Friday, with no signs that market tensions would ease in the near future.
"There is not much likelihood things will change until Russia starts to deliver," one dealer said.
Talks between Russian export officials and Japanese trading houses -- their largest customers for palladium -- began this week on long-delayed contracts for 1997 shipments.
Spot platinum was indicated around $465.50/500.00 an ounce, after seeing a morning high at $500.00, the highest level since 1990.
Spot palladium was indicated around $225.00 an ounce, after seeing a 17 year high earlier this week.
Russia is the largest exporter of palladium.

Sources close to Japanese businesses here said the Russian material was likely to arrive in Japan in July. Russian officials at the negotiations said they would begin shipments on June 20, having last exported in December.
Barry Davison, managing director of South Africa's Amplats, the world's leading producer of platinum, told Reuters that South African producers did not have stocks to ship to the market.

"I don't believe the South African primary producers have stocks of metal. I don't think relief can come from here. The relief can only come from a resumption of Russian supplies and dishoarding of the metal," he said in an interview.
A meeting of the London Platinum and Palladium Market Association late Thursday confirmed that there had been no delivery defaults in the market.
However, market sources said that could change if the liquidity squeeze continued.
"The Russians could do spot deals into Zurich (the contractual delivery point for platinum and palladium deals) and that would help to alleviate the situation," a dealer said.
He added that there was no indication that was forthcoming.

The only other sources of metal would be sales from the U.S. strategic stockpile or positions on the Nymex and Tokyo Commodity Exchange futures markets being unwound, both of which were unlikely, dealers said.
"As we get further into June, we could see a lot more activity," one dealer said.
The metals are used in electronics, catalysts for cleaning up car exhuast fumes, dental work and jewelry.
Gold and silver prices were both a little firmer, supported by platinum and palladium. Gold fixed at $344.00, up from $340.80 on Thursday, and silver was at $4.88/$4.91, up nine cents.
